deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no mathematical derivation. It is a passage of Riemann's speculative psychology and metaphysics: the 'Geistesmassen' doctrine, continued from Blatt 14 (section 2, 'Reproduction durch Erinnerung und Einbildungskraft') and running on to section 3, 'Erdseele'. The page states a set of qualitative axioms. Paraphrased:

(A1) Once formed, Geistesmassen (units of mental substance created by each elementary act of thought) are imperishable. Their connections cannot be dissolved. Only the relative strength of the connections changes, as new Geistesmassen are added.

(A2) Persistence needs no material carrier. Geistesmassen therefore exert no lasting effect on the phenomenal world, stand in no relation to any part of matter, and have no seat in space.

(A3) Every entry, formation and union of Geistesmassen does require a material carrier. Hence all thinking happens at a definite place.

(A3') Empirical remark in parentheses: retaining experiences costs no effort, only thinking does. The expenditure of force is, as far as we can estimate, proportional to mental activity.

(A4) Each newly forming Geistesmasse connects (enters into interaction), for material causes, with the Geistesmasse formed immediately before it. All masses connected with that one are stimulated to activity, the more strongly the closer the connection.

(A5) Each entering mass stimulates all masses related to it. The stimulation is stronger the smaller the difference of inner state (quality).

(A6) This stimulation also spreads indirectly to masses connected with the related ones, i.e. masses linked to them in earlier thought processes. A subset of related masses that are mutually connected is therefore stimulated both directly and indirectly, and so comparatively more strongly than the rest.

(A7) The interaction of two simultaneously forming masses is conditioned by a material process between the places where they form. The sentence continues on the next page.

A modern reading (mine, not Riemann's) is a weighted associative graph:
- Nodes are Geistesmassen; edge weights w_ij are connection strengths.
- A similarity kernel s_j depends on the qualitative difference d_j from the entering mass and decreases in d.
- Activation is a_j = s_j + sum_k w_jk s_k (direct plus one-step indirect), or more generally a = (I - cW)^{-1} s.

Under this reading, a mutually connected cluster of similar nodes gets extra activation from the indirect terms. That is the qualitative content of A6. Riemann gives no formula; any quantitative form is my interpretation.
errors: No mathematical errors, since no computation is performed.
The parenthetical claim that effort is proportional to mental activity (A3') is an unquantified empirical assertion. Neither quantity is defined.

There is a mild tension between A2 (masses have no relation to any part of matter) and A4/A7 (formation and interaction are materially localized). Riemann resolves it by distinguishing persistence from formation, but the distinction is asserted, not argued.

results.what: Mental units (Geistesmassen) are imperishable with indissoluble connections; only relative connection strengths change.
results.modern_name: Associationist memory model (permanent memory traces with changing weights); cf. Herbartian Vorstellungsmechanik
results.usually_credited_to: Herbart (1824-25) for the Vorstellungsmechanik framework; associationism generally

results.what: Activation spreads from a new mental unit to connected and similar units, decreasing with connection distance and qualitative dissimilarity; mutually connected clusters receive extra (direct plus indirect) activation.
results.usually_credited_to: Collins & Loftus (1975), Quillian (1960s); qualitatively Herbart and the associationists

results.what: Thinking is localized and requires a material (nervous) process; effort is proportional to mental activity.
results.modern_name: Psychophysical parallelism / localization of mental function

deep.surprise_reason: This is part of Riemann's well-known 'Geistesmassen' fragment on psychology and metaphysics. It is printed in the Gesammelte mathematische Werke (Weber/Dedekind 1876; 2nd ed. 1892) among the 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts' ('Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik'). The ideas are qualitative and Herbart-inspired, with no mathematical content.

checkable.sympy: import sympy as sp; W=sp.Matrix([[0,1,0],[1,0,0],[0,0,0]]); s=sp.Matrix([1,1,1]); a=s+W*s; a
checkable.asserts: Illustrative only (my formalization, not Riemann's). With equal direct stimulation, two mutually connected similar nodes get activation 2 each and the isolated node gets 1, matching A6: connected subsets are stimulated more strongly.

checkable.sympy: import sympy as sp; c=sp.Rational(1,2); W=sp.Matrix([[0,1,0],[1,0,0],[0,0,0]]); s=sp.Matrix([1,1,1]); sp.simplify((sp.eye(3)-c*W).inv()*s)
checkable.asserts: Illustrative: with full multi-step spreading at damping 1/2, the connected pair gets activation 2 each versus 1 for the isolated node.

transcription_corrections: The parenthesis opened at '(Die älteren der Seele angehörigen Geistesmassen werden von den sich bildenden, eintretenden zur Wirksamkeit angeregt.' is never closed in the manuscript. This sentence reads as an alternative wording of the preceding paragraph.
Folio markings: top right reads 'Nat. Ph.' and '25.'; the circled '13' stands in the right margin about one-third of the way down. These are archival foliation, not part of the text.
The machine transcription otherwise agrees with the image in all substantive wording I can verify.
